headings.text: Lock in a discount. The chart never notices.
Every bag hangs in public, with its price on the tag.
A deal that closes like a vault door: once, and on a clock.
Escrow takes the bag
A buyer pays the listed price
Each fill cuts a key
That key can change hands
On the date, the lock opens
Dial in a discount. See what the pool would have cost.
Lockers ask holders to wait for nothing. Pools punish anyone with size.
A bag bigger than its pool
Size is hard to buy, too
Nothing on day one
A lock that cannot move
Deals in direct messages
A position is a key with a date stamped into it.
Visible before you buy
Tradable while locked
Claimable by anyone
One fill, one key, one date.
$LORH opens the first ten minutes. It never changes a price.
Every fill buys and burns
Latch the opening minutes
Pin a listing on the rail
Use the token later
What the contract cannot do
The market keeps nothing. Its fees leave as burned $LORH.
Two contracts hold the money. Everything else only reads.
What the contract cannot do
Eight ways to cheat it, and what each one costs.
What is on the bench, and what waits its turn.
A seller can list a bag and a buyer can fill it
$LORH launches and listing #1 opens the same day
More ways to price a locked bag
Other apps start quoting the discount
Decisions, and why each one was made.
The lock is sold as a discount
No early exit; the position is sold instead
Fixed-price listings first
Fee 2% primary, 1% resale
No price feed on the chain
Immutable contracts
What gets measured
Ignored on purpose
Every lock has weak points. These are ours.
A launchpad adds it natively
Sellers do not come
Buyers get hurt
